newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU refinery output falls in December from Nov peak.
newsitem.headline: EU refinery output falls in December from Nov peak.

text.p: Refinery output in the European Union fell by 1.3 percent from its November peak, although with little change in distillate production, Stichting Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.

Total refinery output in the 14 nations of the European Union, excluding Sweden, fell by 160,000 barrels per day (bpd) (1.3 percent) to 12,245 million bpd in December, while refinery crude intake was down 237,000 bpd (2.0 percent) to 11,589 million bpd. This represented a utilisation rate of 91.98 percent, against 93.86 percent in November.
But year-on-year, total output was up 361,000 bpd (3.0 percent).
Middle distillate output was down a mere 22,000 bpd (0.4 percent) in December to 5,531 million bpd. The fall was not concentrated in any one country.
Gasoline production fell 72,000 bpd (2.2 percent) in December to 3,223 million bpd, unchanged from a year ago.
Naphtha output was up 26,000 bpd (2.7 percent) to 994,000 bpd, 111,000 bpd (12.6 percent) higher than in December 1995.
The full results are based on a nameplate capacity of 12.6 million bpd. Refinery intake represents crude only and excludes natural gas liquids, feedstocks and other inputs.
